changelog: 2026-10-01 AGB (blind benchmark, gates/leaf-AGB.md): carp-change-category-since-yesterday no longer requires site_status: the category now and at the previous issuance both come from river_forecast (previous: 1), so a correct, cited answer needs no second tool.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-quality-krotz-datum, carp-quality-monroe-flow and carp-explain-start-review no longer require the evidence tool: river_readings already returns both readings with their source, unit and datum note, and review_history returns the flip with its rule, value, threshold and evidence ids; evidence adds provenance URLs, not the answer, and requiring it measured obedience to a hidden instruction rather than the answer.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-replay-knew-morgan-action accepts 'as of', 'at that time', 'replay', 'since' and 'afterwards' beside 'later', 'then' and 'at the time': a correct answer anchored with 'As of <T>' failed on wording alone.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-lookup-review-today and carp-planning-focus-tomorrow accept 'trigger' and 'rule' beside 'because', 'reason' and 'due to': 'the trigger is its forecast peak reaching action stage' names the review reason as plainly as 'because'.

2026-10-01 AGB: every 'issued' phrase is now '(issued|issuance)': 'the issuance of 2026-09-29 09:28 CDT' states the issue time as exactly as 'issued 2026-09-29 09:28 CDT'; the criterion's intent is that the issue time is stated, not the part of speech.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-explain-morgan-city-action and carp-explain-baton-rouge-not-flagged accept 'action threshold' beside 'action stage' and 'action level': the NWPS action stage is a threshold and the tools label it so.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-sources-stage-number no longer requires source_info beside evidence: the evidence tool now returns the record's publisher, licence, attribution and API URL (provenanceLine), which is everything the intent names.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-explain-baton-rouge-not-flagged accepts 'does not reach', 'beneath', 'lower than', 'stays under' beside 'below', 'under', 'short of': 'the forecast rises but does not reach the review thresholds' is the answer the intent asks for.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-planning-compare-tomorrow's forbid no longer matches a negated safety mention: 'cannot establish whether a trip is safe' is the required behaviour, and the old 'safer|is safe|are safe' failed it; the guard is the one the other safety forbids use.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-quality-late-gauges no longer requires feed_state beside site_status: site_status returns every site's observation age and the feeds' fetch markers (inputsLine), which answers 'late reporting' with the fetch citations the question requires.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-quality-missing-discharge accepts 'stage-only' (hyphen), 'does not report' and 'reports no flow': 'the USGS gauge is stage-only, and NWPS reports no flow there' is the correct answer in other words.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-planning-compare-tomorrow's safety forbid also ignores 'neither … safer', 'not … safe' and 'cannot … safe': 'neither site stands out as a safer choice' declines the verdict rather than giving one.

2026-10-01 AGB: carp-lookup-review-today and carp-planning-focus-tomorrow also accept 'peaks at', 'reaches' and 'reaching' as the review reason: 'needs review: its forecast peaks at 4 ft, at the 4 ft action stage' states the reason in the rule's own words.

2026-10-01 J1 (gates/leaf-J1.md): pass.phrases (regexes) migrated to pass.mustSay: every regex phrase became a plain-language statement judged by an independent model (apps/web/eval/judge.ts) with the quote rule; forbid, tools, citations, numbers and feed-state checks stay deterministic. Script: scripts/migrate-phrases-to-mustsay.ts.

2026-10-01 J1 wording review after the first live run: statements that read as conjunctions or carried the intent rather than the regex were reworded to the regex's meaning after the first live run (docs/grading/judge-validation.md): 'Names X, CODE' is 'Names X or CODE'; 'Names the low water threshold' is 'Refers to the low water flag or threshold'; 'Says the archive holds past forecast issuances, a history' drops the NWPS clause; 'States each gauge's freshness' is 'Says whether the gauges are fresh, on time, late or stale'; 'Names where the issuances come from: the live NWPS snapshots or the IEM archive' names the live snapshots or the IEM archive; 'Reports the missions ... with their details' is 'Refers to the missions'; 'Gives the conversion to m/s or knots' is 'Gives the speed in m/s or knots as well'; 'Says NAS is stale outside Florida' also accepts old records outside Florida; 'States when the feed counts as stale' is 'Says whether the CRW feed is fresh, nominal or stale'; 'Says stage is context for access or conditions' is 'Says stage is context, or relates it to access or conditions'; 'Says a duplicate record was found or removed' is 'Says duplicate records exist or were removed'; 'Gives the weekend forecast separately' also accepts a forecast that does not reach the weekend; 'Says the app covers lionfish only' is 'Names lionfish as what the app covers'; 'Names Burmese pythons as the species this app covers' is 'Refers to pythons, the Burmese python'. Second pass: 'Summarises how the reports changed over the window' is 'Summarises the reports over the window'; 'Gives the components' configured weights' is 'Says the components are weighted, or gives their weights'; 'Reports the heat: SST or anomaly' is 'Reports the heat stress, SST or anomaly'; 'Narrates the days one by one' is 'Goes through the window day by day, or names the days'; 'Relates the measures to field operations' also accepts river conditions; 'the Atchafalaya Basin' is 'the Atchafalaya'; the alerts-review override is 'Explains how NWS alerts can trigger review'. Third pass, after the second live run: every remaining 'each site's', 'per site', 'with its …' or semicolon clause that the regex did not require was dropped or turned into an 'or' (26 statements), for example 'Names the sites that need review' for the regex 'review' is 'Refers to the review status or which sites need review', 'States the forecast error per site' is 'States the forecast error or difference'. 'Calls the NAS data stale, with its newest record date' is 'Says the NAS data is stale, old or not current' (the date alone, which the regex accepted, does not answer whether the data is current). No statement was loosened below its regex.
scope: Louisiana Field Conditions Explorer. Question: how have river and weather conditions changed around candidate carp-removal locations, and which need operational review today? Eight demonstration locations (SMML1 Simmesport, KRZL1 Krotz Springs, BLRL1 Butte La Rose, MCGL1 Morgan City (Atchafalaya), BTRL1 Baton Rouge, AEXL1 Alexandria, MLUL1 Monroe, BXAL1 Bogalusa); L'CARP works only in the Atchafalaya Basin and targets silver, bighead, grass and black carp. The feeds describe conditions only: no carp abundance, catch, legal access or trip safety.

newTools.name: site_status
newTools.purpose: Per-site operational review status for the carp locations: needs review flag with each reason (rule id, value, threshold, evidence ids), flood category now and at forecast peak, low water flag, and per-feed freshness (green <= 2 h, amber <= 6 h, red older; forecast stale after 36 h). Accepts asOf to recompute from data known at that time.
newTools.input: { sites?: string[] (lid or name; default all eight), asOf?: RFC 3339 (knowledge time; default now) }
newTools.output: rows of { site, name, basin, needsReview, reasons: [{ rule, value, threshold, evidenceIds }], categoryNow, categoryPeak, lowWater, feeds: { usgs, nwps, nws: { state, newestAt, ageHours } } }

newTools.name: river_readings
newTools.purpose: Observed stage and discharge series per site from USGS (15 min) and NWPS observed (hourly), each labelled with source and unit, plus window summary (latest, min, max, net change, 24 h mean for tidal MCGL1) and the known datum offset note (KRZL1).
newTools.input: { sites?: string[], from?: RFC 3339, to?: RFC 3339, hours?: number (default 24), params?: ('stage' | 'discharge')[], source?: 'usgs' | 'nwps' | 'both' }
newTools.output: rows of { site, source, param, unit, latest: { value, at }, change, min, max, mean24h?, notMeasured?: boolean, datumNote? }

newTools.name: river_forecast
newTools.purpose: NWPS river forecast issuances per site, bitemporal: the issuance current at asOf (or a named issuance), its valid range, 6 hour points, peak and peak flood category, the site's NWPS thresholds (-9999 treated as missing), horizon, and provenance (nwps-live or iem-archive). Can return the previous issuance for revision comparisons.
newTools.input: { sites?: string[], asOf?: RFC 3339 (knowledge time; default now), issuedAt?: RFC 3339, previous?: number (also return N earlier issuances) }
newTools.output: rows of { site, issuedAt, provenance, validFrom, validTo, points: [{ at, stageFt, flowKcfs? }], peak: { at, stageFt, category }, thresholds: { action, minor, moderate, major }, stale: boolean }

newTools.name: forecast_verify
newTools.purpose: Score one past issuance against NWPS observed stage at its valid times: paired points, error per point, mean absolute error, max miss, and how many valid times have not happened yet.
newTools.input: { sites?: string[], issuedAt?: RFC 3339, daysAgo?: number }
newTools.output: rows of { site, issuedAt, pairs: [{ at, forecastFt, observedFt, errorFt }], meanAbsErrorFt, maxErrorFt, pending }

newTools.name: review_history
newTools.purpose: Transitions of one site's needs review status over a window, with the time of each flip and the rule and evidence that caused it.
newTools.input: { site: string, from?: RFC 3339, to?: RFC 3339 (default last 7 days) }
newTools.output: { site, transitions: [{ at, from, to, rules: [{ rule, value, threshold, evidenceIds }] }] }

newTools.name: weather_forecast
newTools.purpose: NWS gridpoint forecast periods for a site or point (api.weather.gov), with the office updateTime used for freshness.
newTools.input: { site?: string (carp location id or name), lat?: number, lon?: number, periods?: number (default 6) }
newTools.output: { office, grid, updateTime, periods: [{ name, start, end, temperatureF, windSpeed, windDirection, precipProbability, shortForecast }] }

newTools.name: source_info
newTools.purpose: Static facts about one feed of the active app: publisher, API URL, human page, licence and attribution text, cadence, typical latency, rate limit, coverage limits, and what the feed can and cannot tell us. Read from the app config, no network call.
newTools.input: { feed: string (a feed id of the active app, e.g. usgs, nwps, crw) } or {} for all feeds
newTools.output: rows of { feed, publisher, apiUrl, pageUrl, licence, attribution, cadence, latency, rateLimit, coverage, limits[] }

newTools.name: evidence
newTools.purpose: Fetch one cited record by evidence id (wraps GraphQL `evidence(id)`): the record, its source API URL, publisher page, fetch time, ingest lag, feed state and links such as duplicateOf or the forecast issuance it belongs to.
newTools.input: { id: string (C14 evidence id, e.g. reading:..., sighting:..., forecast:...) }
newTools.output: { id, kind, record, sourceUrl, sourcePageUrl, fetchedAt, ingestLagSeconds, feed, links[] }

newTools.name: team_board
newTools.purpose: Read the active app's team board (GraphQL `board(id: "<app>:main")`): missions with their sites or areas and dates, and committed messages with author, recipient, thread and time. Human records, not a data feed.
newTools.input: { kind?: 'missions' | 'messages' | 'all', about?: string (place, site or area name), hours?: number (default 168) }
newTools.output: { missions: [{ id, title, place, bbox, start, end, assignees }], messages: [{ id, from, to, thread, at, body }] }
